# Gitslice

> Gitslice is Git-compatible source infrastructure for humans and coding agents.
> Work happens in a workspace bound to one slice (a repo-like view of a global
> codebase); edits become changesets that are submitted and published as
> commits. Agents can sign themselves up. No browser or human is needed.

## For agents: get started in four commands

1. Install the `gs` CLI (prebuilt for Linux and macOS, amd64 and arm64; no Go
   toolchain needed, checksum-verified):

       curl -fsSL https://gitslice.io/install.sh | sh

   It installs to ~/.local/bin (override with GS_INSTALL_DIR). Windows and
   other builds: https://github.com/gitslice-io/gitslice/releases/latest
   With Go 1.24+ you can instead run:
   `go install github.com/gitslice-io/gitslice/cmd/gs@latest`

2. Register yourself. This creates your own account and home slice, and saves a
   long-lived API key as your CLI credential. Use the email of the human you
   work for: they can later claim co-ownership of what you create.

       gs auth register-agent --username <your-agent-name> --email <owner-email>

   Optional: `--display-name "Release bot"`. Username rules: 4-63 characters of
   lowercase letters, digits and '-' ('_' becomes '-'), not starting or ending
   with '-', unique, and not reserved. The CLI checks them before contacting the
   server. The key is never printed. Run `gs auth token` only if a script truly
   needs it, and never share it.

   Safe to retry: if registration times out or the connection drops, run the
   exact same command again. It resumes the same registration instead of
   failing because the username is now taken.

   On success it prints the claim link and steps to send your human owner.

3. Check that you are signed in:

       gs auth status --json

4. Do work in your home slice (`<your-agent-name>:home`, path `/<your-agent-name>`):

       mkdir work && cd work
       gs init <your-agent-name>:home
       echo "hello" > <your-agent-name>/HELLO.md
       gs status
       gs create --all --message "My first change"
       gs submit
       gs fs cat /<your-agent-name>/HELLO.md

   `gs submit` queues the changeset for publishing; it becomes a commit within
   seconds. Most commands accept `--json` for structured output.

## For the human owner

Open https://gitslice.io/claims and sign in with the email the agent
registered (it must be verified). Click Accept to become a co-owner; the agent
keeps its access. Its slices then appear on your home page next to yours.
From a terminal: `gs auth login`, then `gs claims list` and
`gs claims accept <agent-subject-id>`.

## Visibility

New slices, including an agent's home slice, are private: only signed-in
members of the account can open them in the browser. `gs browse --print` warns
when a link points at a private slice. To share one:
`gs slice update <account>:<slice> --visibility public`.

## Limits

- Registration is rate limited per client IP (currently 5 per hour).
- The server is `api.gitslice.io:443` by default; pass `--server` to use another.

## More

- Docs: https://gitslice.io/doc
- Agents guide: https://gitslice.io/doc/agents
- CLI reference: https://gitslice.io/doc/cli
